title: Corner stop compares only neighbouring street lines, so a rounded corner drawn as several short lines is never caught: a 40 ft lot reads 195.6 ft wide and complies
detail: Lot._turn returns only the sharpest turn between two neighbouring street lot lines, so the stop fires only when one step turns more than 30 degrees. Tax-map and GIS outlines draw a corner's curb-return arc as several straight pieces, and both the plugin (_segments uses DuplicateSegments) and read_3dm (_edges) make each piece its own edge. A 90 degree corner drawn as four 22.5 degree steps, or as three 30 degree steps (the test is a strict >), never trips the stop. The lot is then measured along both streets, which is the exact P0 this round says it fixed. rhino_logic.one_street uses the same pairwise test, so layer (b) also keeps both streets' lines across such a corner. Reproduced: a 40 x 160 lot with the corner at (40,0) rounded at radius 10 in 4 pieces; street_line = the bottom line, the 4 arc pieces and the east line; corner_lot False. check_site reports Lot width complies, measured at 195.607 ft (the same lot fails at 40 ft with the bottom line alone). Lot._turn = 22.5 and one_street = True. This is reachable today: through facts saved in a .3dm before round 5 (the old bug kept both streets after a No answer), or through any multi-line street_line such as the sample's or a future lookup's. Layer (c) is described as the safety net 'whatever the lot was answered', and here it does not hold.
evidence: measure.py:120 `elif facts.get("corner_lot") is not True and self._turn(street) > STREET_TURN_DEG:`; _turn compares pairs only: `for i, j in zip(chain, chain[1:]): ... most = max(most, math.degrees(math.acos(...)))`. rhino_logic.one_street has the same pairwise test: `for (a, b), (c, d) in zip(lines, lines[1:]): ... if math.degrees(math.acos(cos)) > STREET_TURN_DEG: return False`. Script output: `turn 22.500000000000018`, `width 195.607226 None`, `one_street True`, `Lot width complies`.
pin: packages/design_checker/tests/test_check.py, beside test_a_corner_lot_answered_no_never_keeps_both_streets...: a 40 x 160 lot whose corner is a radius-10 arc in 4 straight pieces (22.5 degrees each), plus a variant with three 30 degree steps. With all 6 (or 5) street lines and corner_lot False, assert the Lot width item is not 'complies', measurements['lot_width'].reason contains 'turn a corner', and logic.one_street(lines) is False. Both must fail with the current pairwise _turn and one_street.
suggested_fix: Measure the street's whole change of direction, not the largest single step. Sum the signed heading changes along the ordered chain (or take the largest angle between any two street lines' directions) and stop when that total exceeds STREET_TURN_DEG. Put the computation in one shared function that both Lot._turn and rhino_logic.one_street call, so the measuring and the box cannot disagree. 106 Ithaca Rd's eight lines stay within about 4 degrees in total (headings -179.5 to 176.1), so the sample is unaffected.

In packages/model_measurement/model_measurement/measure.py, line 120 (added in this diff) fires the corner stop only when `self._turn(street) > STREET_TURN_DEG`. `_turn` (lines 125-138) compares only consecutive street edges (`zip(chain, chain[1:])`) and keeps the largest single turn. It never adds up the turns along the street or compares the overall direction. So a 90-degree corner drawn as four 22.5-degree pieces never trips it. packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:787-812 `one_street` uses the same pairwise test against STREET_TURN_DEG. I found no other check upstream: before line 120, Lot.__init__ only tests no_street, street_not_a_lot_line, street_lines_apart and all_street. My repro used the repo's .venv Python with the 106_ithaca_rd facts: a 40 x 160 lot with the (40,0) corner rounded at radius 10 in 4 pieces, street_line set to the bottom line, the 4 arc pieces and the east line, and corner_lot False. Output: `turn 22.5, street_problem None`, `one_street True`, `lot_width 195.607226, reason None`, and check_site's view gives `Lot width complies`. That is a false pass, which breaks principle 4. The stop is new code in this diff (origin/rhino-ui had no corner stop at all), so this is an incomplete fix of the round-5 P0 rather than a pre-existing issue. To reach it, a street_line has to be stated with several lines that turn a corner through small steps. The data model allows that, because facts accept any list of lot lines that touch end to end.

title: corner_answered treats the first answer (unanswered to No) as a change and wipes the box's prefilled street line and the looked-up street name
detail: The start box now runs every Apply and every Draw through logic.corner_answered. corner_answered calls after_corner_answer(facts, was), which drops street_line whenever the answer differs from the stored one. suggested_facts always stores corner_lot None ('never guessed'), so the architect's first answer (Not answered to No) counts as a change. The prefilled blue front lot line and the saved street_name are deleted. In the main flow (empty file, prefilled box, answer Corner lot? No, Draw) the checker gets no street line. Lot width, front, side and rear yards all go to needs review ('the street side isn't given'), and the largest-legal-building step has no street. At 1ceab82, _apply_box only set corner_lot, so this is a regression from fix (a). The pin test covers only True to False and True to None, never None to False. The in-Rhino quickstart sets corner_lot through setfacts, not the box, so it does not catch this either.
evidence: rhino_logic.corner_answered: `was = (facts or {}).get("corner_lot")` ... `facts = after_corner_answer(facts, was)`; after_corner_answer: `if out.get("corner_lot") != was_corner: out.pop("street_line", None)`; suggested_facts: `facts["corner_lot"] = None  # never guessed`. Ran: corner_answered(suggested_facts(... lowest line [[0,0],[40,0]] ...), {'street_name':'Ithaca Rd'}, False) returns facts without 'street_line' and saved_ui {}. gordium_rhino._apply_box line 1260 and _drawn line 1391 call it on every Draw.
pin: packages/design_checker/tests/test_check.py: f = logic.suggested_facts(...) with one prefilled street line, then logic.corner_answered(f, {'street_name': 'Ithaca Rd'}, False). Assert street_line is kept, street_name is kept and corner_lot is False. Must fail on the current code.
suggested_fix: Drop the street lines only when a real earlier answer changes: `was is not None and corner != was`. Better still, drop them only when the lines no longer fit the new answer: a non-corner answer keeps them if one_street(lines) holds under the corrected cumulative test, and a Yes keeps the lines already picked and asks for the other street. Keep the street name whenever the lines are kept.

title: The new stop calls a single street that bends more than 30 degrees 'two streets' and tells the architect to pick only one line, and doing that gives a front yard that complies when it fails
detail: The stop says 'that is two streets' as a fact and tells the architect to 'pick only the lot line on the street'. A single street that bends more than 30 degrees at the lot (a bend, a coarse cul-de-sac bulb, or a curved frontage drawn as one arc whose chord sits more than 30 degrees off its straight neighbours) trips it too. If the architect follows the advice, the box's re-pick keeps only the clicked line (one_street is False), so the front yard is measured from part of the street. Reproduced: lot (0,0),(40,0),(70,25),(70,150),(0,150); the street runs (0,0) to (40,0) to (70,25), a 40 degree bend; house box(20,30,50,70). With both lines: everything needs review (the stop). With only the first line, as the stop advises: Front yard complies at 30'-0", and the second street line is treated as a side line ('Side yard, Southeast complies 16'-7 5/8"'). With only the second line, the front yard fails at 16'-7 5/8". Whether the lot faces one bending street or two streets is not settled by the drawing (measure.py itself says the city's corner definition 'has no angle in it'), so the code is guessing, and its remediation leads to a front-yard false pass.
evidence: stops.py: `"street_turns_a_corner": "the street lot lines given turn a corner ({turn}° from one to the next): that is two streets, ... answer Corner lot? or pick only the lot line on the street"`; rhino_logic.street_lines_after_pick: `... and one_street(lines): return [list(map(list, line)) for line in lines]` / `return [picked]`. Script output with street_line [A]: `('Front yard', 'complies', '30\'-0"')`; with [B]: `('Front yard', 'does_not_comply', '16\'-7 5/8"')`.
pin: packages/model_measurement/tests/test_stop_list.py or test_check.py: on the bent-frontage lot above, the stop's wording must not say it 'is two streets' and must not advise picking one line. Also, logic.street_lines_after_pick([A, B], A) on a lot answered No must not shrink the street to [A] without the architect's explicit statement that B is not on the street.
suggested_fix: Word the stop as an open question: 'the street lot lines turn {turn}°: a corner (two streets) or one street that bends? Answer Corner lot?'. Do not tell the architect to drop lines. When a lot answered No has turning lines, keep the whole set and the stop until the architect states the street lines themselves, and record that statement. Never shrink to a single clicked line on the strength of a geometric guess.

What I read:

- stops.py:28-30 (new). The message says "that is two streets" as a fact and tells the architect to "pick only the lot line on the street".
- The README already says a corner lot is "never guessed from the drawing (the city's definition has no angle in it)". This rule is a guess from the drawing.
- rhino_logic.py street_lines_after_pick and one_street (both new). A re-pick keeps the whole street only when one_street(lines) is true, and one_street is false above 30°. Otherwise it returns [picked], so a re-pick keeps only the one line clicked.

I re-ran the finding's example myself, calling measure() with the test_measure helpers:
- Lot: (0,0),(40,0),(70,25),(70,150),(0,150).
- House: box(20,30,50,70).
- corner_lot: False.

Results:
- Both street lines: every yard stops with the 40° "turn a corner" reason, so all need review.
- Only line A, as the message advises: front_yard = 30.0. Line B becomes a side line (side_yard_smaller = 16.64).
- Only line B: front_yard = 16.64.

So if one street bends 40° at this lot, following the advice measures the front yard from part of the street. It reads 30 ft when the true distance is 16.6 ft, which is a false pass.

Nothing upstream stops this. Per the git diff, the old code measured from both lines together (16.6 ft, correct for one bending street). The new stop and its advice lead the architect into the bad case.

I could not refute this. I reproduced it at 8e3582f.

What the code does:
- measure.py, in Lot.__init__ (the added `elif` and `_turn`): when the lot is not answered as a corner lot and its street lines turn more than STREET_TURN_DEG (30°) from one to the next, it gives the new `street_turns_a_corner` stop.
- That stop's text (stops.py:28-30) says flatly "that is two streets" and offers "pick only the lot line on the street" as one way out.
- rhino_logic.py:771-784, street_lines_after_pick, keeps the whole set of street lines only if `one_street(lines)` is true. one_street (rhino_logic.py:787+) is new in this PR (git grep finds no one_street on origin/rhino-ui) and fails on any turn of 30° or more. In that case the function returns `[picked]`, only the one line clicked.
- gordium_rhino.py:1325 is the box's re-pick path for a lot that is not a corner, and it calls that function.

So for a single street that bends more than 30°, following the stop's advice keeps one line of the street. Nothing upstream stops this: the turn check uses only angles, and nothing checks whether the lines are really one street.

Reproduction: check_site with the test helpers. Lot (0,0),(40,0),(70,25),(70,150),(0,150), house box(20,30,50,70), corner_lot=False.
- Both lines: every yard row needs review.
- Only line A: Front yard complies at 30'-0", and Side yard, Southeast complies at 16'-7 5/8". That side line is the second street line.
- Only line B: Front yard does not comply at 16'-7 5/8".

The front yard therefore passes while the house sits 16'-7 5/8" from part of the street: a false pass on that row. Lot width still fails in this example, so the lot as a whole doesn't pass, but the front-yard row does.

Whether a bend like this is one street or two is not settled by the geometry; measure.py itself notes the city's corner definition has no angle in it. The PR's new stop plus its new one_street re-pick logic are what lead the architect into this outcome. Before this PR, the re-pick kept all the street lines. So this is introduced by the PR, not pre-existing.

title: _drawn_advice passes the hint sentence as the row name, and its yard branch can never be used
detail: _drawn_advice calls `_yard_advice("To comply", hint, m, ...)`. The second argument is the row name, which _yard_line reads for the compass side, but here it gets the hint sentence. A side yard's line therefore always comes out as 'that side lot line'. The yard advice it builds also never equals the row's hint (_hint says 'move the building X farther from that lot line'). So `"_advice": advice if hint and advice and hint == advice_text(advice) else None` is always None for a yard, and confirm_advice then sets the hint to None. The branch is dead, and it carries the very move-the-building wording this round set out to replace.
evidence: present.py:495 `return _yard_advice("To comply", hint, m, values[m], -margin, ...)`; _hint: `return f"To comply: move the building {gap} farther from that lot line."`. Ran: _hint('Side yard, West', ...) = 'To comply: move the building 3'-0" farther from that lot line.'; advice_text(_drawn_advice(...)) = '... from that side lot line — now 7'-0" at its closest.'; equal == False.
pin: packages/design_checker/tests/test_present.py: for a failing side yard 'Side yard, West' with no reading set, the row's _advice is not None, its hint names 'the west side lot line', and the hint equals advice_text(_advice). Fails today.
suggested_fix: Pass the row label to _drawn_advice (label, not hint), and set the yard row's hint to advice_text(advice) when _drawn_advice returns yard advice. Otherwise delete the yard branch and the _hint yard wording.

A hint sentence never yields a COMPASS word there, so a side yard always gets "that side lot line".

2. **The yard advice is always thrown away.** For a yard, `_hint` (present.py:333-334) returns "To comply: move the building {gap} farther from that lot line." `advice_text` for advice that carries `yard` (present.py:513-519) returns "To comply: keep every part of the building at least ... — now ... at its closest". These two strings can never be equal. So the gate at present.py:1088, `advice if hint and advice and hint == advice_text(advice) else None`, always gives None for a yard row, and the advice _drawn_advice built is discarded.

3. **The hint is then cleared.** check.confirm_advice (check.py:248-252) pops `_advice`, and with none present it sets a "To comply" hint to None.

One mitigating point: settle's comply_hint path (present.py:812-826) can later replace the hint and advice for some failing yards. That does not bring the drawn yard branch back to life, so the finding stands as a P3 dead-code and wording issue.
